blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine family law should look beyond traditional labels of legitimacy and give greater weight to the actual circumstances and best interests of children, a legal scholar and human rights advocate said. Ateneo de Manila University professor Atty. Amparita S. Sta. Maria raised the issue at the opening of the university’s new “Ateneo Breakthroughs Lectures” series, where she discussed how laws governing legitimacy can create a gap between a child’s lived family relationships and those recognized by law.
